questions.question: Define electrolysis. Then draw up a comparison of galvanic and electrolytic cells under the headings energy conversion, spontaneity and electrode polarity, and list the statements that remain true in both cell types.
questions.expected_answer: Electrolysis is the chemical process in which electrical energy is used to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction. Comparison: (1) Energy conversion — galvanic cells convert chemical energy into electrical energy; electrolytic cells convert electrical energy into chemical energy supplied by an external power source. (2) Spontaneity — the galvanic reaction is spontaneous; the electrolytic reaction is non-spontaneous and must be forced. (3) Polarity — the galvanic anode is negative and its cathode positive; the electrolytic anode is positive (attached to the positive terminal of the supply) and its cathode negative. True in both: oxidation occurs at the anode, reduction occurs at the cathode, the electrolyte conducts by the movement of ions, and anions migrate to the anode while cations migrate to the cathode.

questions.question: For the electrolysis of copper(II) chloride solution with inert carbon electrodes, give the half-reaction and the visible observation at each electrode, the net equation, and the reason the solution's colour fades. Then state the full arrangement — electrodes and electrolyte — needed to silver-plate a brass bangle, with the half-reaction at each electrode.
questions.expected_answer: Cathode (negative): Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu; a pink-brown layer of copper metal builds up on the rod. Anode (positive): 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻; pale bubbles of chlorine gas with a sharp, stinging smell. Net equation: Cu²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ → Cu + Cl₂ — the compound is decomposed into its elements using electrical energy, the carbon rods being inert and contributing no atoms. The blue-green colour fades because the Cu²⁺ ions that cause it are progressively plated out of the solution. Silver plating: the bangle is the cathode on the negative terminal, a silver bar is the anode on the positive terminal, and the electrolyte is a silver ion solution such as silver nitrate. Anode: Ag → Ag⁺ + e⁻ (the bar dissolves and keeps the bath concentration constant); cathode: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag (silver deposits on the bangle). Plating is done for corrosion protection and appearance.

questions.question: For the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution, write the half-reaction at each electrode, explain the outcome of the competition with water at each one, name the three products with one use each, and state what changes at the anode if the brine becomes dilute.
questions.expected_answer: Anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻; in concentrated brine the very high chloride concentration lets chloride out-compete water, so chlorine gas forms. Cathode: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻; the sodium ion is among the hardest cations to reduce — sodium metal is far too reactive to form in water — so water is reduced preferentially and hydrogen gas forms. The remaining Na⁺ ions pair with the OH⁻ ions produced, leaving sodium hydroxide in solution. Products and uses: chlorine — disinfecting drinking and pool water, bleach, PVC manufacture; hydrogen — fuel, hardening oils, ammonia synthesis; sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) — soap, paper and textile manufacture. In dilute solution water out-competes chloride at the anode and oxygen gas forms instead of chlorine, which is why industry keeps the brine concentrated.
